arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-01.question: Your employer wants to charge employees for the cost of new protective gloves they are required to wear. Is this allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as the cost is calculated proportionally and transparently
options.b: Yes, if the works council agrees
options.c: No, the law does not allow the employer to pass the cost of occupational safety measures on to employees
options.d: No, unless the gloves cost more than 20 euros each

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-01.explanation: The German Occupational Safety Act makes clear that protective equipment and other safety measures are the employer's responsibility, including financially. Employees may not be charged for measures meant to protect their own safety and health at work - regardless of the price or whether the works council agrees.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-02.question: A colleague finds the mandatory safety goggles at the workbench annoying and prefers to work without them. How does this stand under employees' legal duties?

options.a: Not a problem, as long as nothing has happened so far
options.b: He is violating his legal duty to properly use the personal protective equipment made available to him
options.c: That is solely the concern of the safety officer, not of the employee themselves
options.d: It is acceptable because only the employer is responsible for provision, not for use

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-02.explanation: Employees are legally required to properly use machines, tools, protective devices, and the personal protective equipment provided to them. The employer must supply the PPE, but using it correctly day to day is each individual's own responsibility - and that is exactly what protects your eyes in an actual accident.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-03.question: A strong smell of gas suddenly fills the production hall and an alarm sounds - an immediate serious danger. What applies to employees in this situation?

options.a: They may leave the workplace immediately to bring themselves to safety, and this may not be held against them in any way
options.b: They must first get their supervisor's permission before leaving the workplace
options.c: They may only leave the workplace if the works fire brigade explicitly orders it
options.d: Leaving is only legally protected once a fire has actually broken out, not merely at the smell of gas

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-03.explanation: German occupational safety law explicitly gives employees the right, in the face of immediate serious danger to safety and health, to bring themselves to safety by leaving the workplace at once - without needing prior permission and without this being held against them. The employer must in fact make this possible in the first place, for example through working escape routes and an alarm system.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-04.question: In a warehouse, one area is loud because a machine is running without any sound insulation. Which order of measures matches the general principles of occupational safety?

options.a: Immediately issue hearing protection to everyone; technical changes to the machine are a secondary concern
options.b: Only relocate the employees most affected, leaving everything else unchanged
options.c: Wait and see if anyone complains about the noise before doing anything at all
options.d: First check whether the noise can be reduced technically at the source (e.g. enclosing the machine); only use personal protective equipment like ear protection if that is not enough

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-04.explanation: The general principles of occupational safety require hazards to be tackled at their source wherever possible, with individual protective measures like personal protective equipment used only as a last resort, once technical and organizational measures cannot sufficiently eliminate the risk. Hearing protection is therefore not the first line of defense, but the last.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-01.question: A new colleague in her department is assigned a new machine she has never worked on before. By when must an instruction on this be given at the latest?

options.a: Only after the six-month probationary period ends
options.b: Before the new machine is used for the first time, tailored to this specific workstation and the new equipment
options.c: Only once the annual department-wide group instruction session is due
options.d: Only if there has already been an accident involving similar machines

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-01.explanation: The duty to instruct employees is not limited to the start of employment - it explicitly also applies whenever job duties change or new equipment or technology is introduced. Before someone uses a new piece of equipment for the first time, they must receive instruction tailored to that specific workstation, regardless of any probation period or the annual schedule.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-02.question: A company held its last general safety instruction exactly 13 months ago, and nothing about the tasks, equipment, or hazards has changed since. Does this meet the requirements?

options.a: Yes, since nothing about the tasks has changed since the last instruction, no new one is needed
options.b: Yes, because a repeat instruction is only required after a workplace accident
options.c: No, the repeat instruction must happen at least once a year regardless of whether anything changed - the deadline has already passed here
options.d: No, but it is sufficient to catch up on the instruction within the next two years

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-02.explanation: In addition to the trigger-based requirement (new tasks, new equipment, new hazards), the relevant accident-prevention regulation sets a fixed minimum frequency: instruction must be repeated as needed, but at least once a year. An unchanged workplace does not exempt anyone from this annual repetition.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-03.question: What is the employer required to do after carrying out a safety instruction session?

options.a: Document the content and date of the instruction, so that compliance with the duty can be proven afterwards
options.b: Nothing further - a purely verbal instruction with no record at all is always sufficient on its own
options.c: Have the instruction session notarized
options.d: It is enough that the instruction took place, regardless of whether it can later be established who attended

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-03.explanation: Instruction must be documented so that, in a dispute or during an inspection - for example after an accident or an authority check - it can be proven who was instructed on what topic and when. No formal notarization is required; a simple instruction record signed by the attendee is the common approach.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-04.question: A company assigns a temporary agency worker and an intern to production work for two weeks. Do both of them also need to receive workplace-specific safety instruction?

options.a: No, the duty to instruct only applies to permanent, full-time employees
options.b: Yes, the duty to instruct applies to everyone deployed in the workplace, regardless of contract type or duration - for the agency worker, this duty falls on the host company using their labor
options.c: No, for agency workers only the staffing agency remains responsible; the host company has no duty at all
options.d: Yes, but only the intern needs to be instructed; an exception applies to agency workers

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-04.explanation: The definition of "employee" under German occupational safety law is broad and explicitly includes interns and temporary agency workers. For agency work, the duty to give workplace-specific instruction rests with the company that actually deploys the worker (the host company) - the staffing agency's separate general duties remain in place but do not substitute for this.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: What is the basic purpose of the risk assessment (Gefährdungsbeurteilung) under German occupational safety law?

options.a: A purely formal document for the accident insurer with no real practical effect on daily work
options.b: A one-time stocktake that is only needed when a company is founded
options.c: The systematic identification of hazards connected with the work, in order to determine which occupational safety measures are actually necessary
options.d: An assessment that exclusively covers psychological strain in the workplace

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must determine which protective measures are necessary by assessing the hazards connected with the work. This is not a one-off administrative box-tick, but the technical basis for concrete decisions - from choosing machinery to organizing work to selecting PPE. Psychological strain is just one of several factors to be considered, not the sole subject of the assessment.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: Which of the following statements about possible causes of hazards under German occupational safety law is NOT correct?

options.a: The design and setup of workplaces and work premises can constitute a hazard
options.b: Physical, chemical, and biological exposures count among possible sources of hazard
options.c: Psychological strain at work must also be considered as a possible hazard
options.d: Only directly visible technical defects in machinery count as a hazard; organizational aspects such as work processes play no role

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The law explicitly lists several sources of hazard, including workplace design, physical/chemical/biological exposures, the design of work equipment, work processes and working hours, insufficient qualification, and psychological strain. Organizational factors such as work processes are explicitly included, not excluded.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: An employee notices an obvious defect in a safety guard that constitutes an immediate serious danger. How should they behave under the law?

options.a: Wait until the next scheduled safety inspection and raise the defect then
options.b: They are required to report the defect to the employer or the responsible supervisor without delay
options.c: Repair the defect themselves to save time, even without the appropriate qualification
options.d: Ignore the incident, as long as the machine still outwardly appears to work normally despite the defect

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: Employees have a specific duty to report: any immediate serious danger to safety and health they identify, as well as any defect they find in protective systems, must be reported without delay. Fixing it themselves without the right qualification, or waiting for the next routine inspection, both conflict with this duty and can prolong the danger for everyone involved.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: A warehouse introduces a new, significantly faster picking system using driverless transport vehicles. What follows for the existing risk assessment?

options.a: It must be reviewed and updated as needed, because the working conditions - and therefore the hazard situation - have changed substantially
options.b: Nothing - the original risk assessment remains valid until a statutory five-year deadline expires
options.c: Nothing - risk assessments only need to be created when a business first opens
options.d: It only needs to be adjusted once an accident involving the new vehicles has already occurred

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: There is no fixed statutory deadline, such as five years, after which a risk assessment automatically expires. Instead, whenever working conditions change substantially - for example through new equipment, new vehicles, or changed processes - the assessment must be reviewed and updated as needed, and this should happen before an accident reveals that it was out of date.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-01.question: You notice that your mandatory hearing protection is damaged and its noise reduction has clearly worsened as a result. How should you respond?

options.a: Keep using it as long as you can still feel some damping material
options.b: Stop using the damaged protective equipment and inform your employer so replacement equipment can be provided
options.c: Improvise yourself with tape to bridge the time until the next order arrives
options.d: Simply swap the damaged hearing protection for a private earplug of unknown origin

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-01.explanation: Personal protective equipment only protects if it actually still works properly. Employees must use the PPE provided to them as intended - continuing to use damaged equipment or improvising a replacement yourself defeats that purpose. A noticed defect in protective equipment should be reported so the employer can arrange a proper replacement.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-02.question: A large moving box has been sitting for several days directly in front of a door marked as an escape route in an office corridor. How should this be assessed?

options.a: Not a problem, as long as the box could quickly be pushed aside if needed
options.b: Acceptable, as long as a second escape route still exists somewhere in the building
options.c: Not acceptable - escape routes and emergency exits must remain fully clear and usable at their full width at all times
options.d: Acceptable, as long as the box is not made of flammable material

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-02.explanation: Escape routes and emergency exits must be kept clear at all times, so that in an emergency - for example fire or smoke - everyone can leave the building quickly and without obstruction. An object blocking an escape door or narrowing the escape route is a safety risk regardless of whether it is flammable, even if a second escape route exists.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-03.question: In an office kitchen, oil in a pan on the stove catches fire. Why is a conventional water fire extinguisher a poor choice here?

options.a: Fires involving fats/oils belong to their own fire class, where water can actually make things worse by causing a fat explosion/fireball - special extinguishing agents are needed instead
options.b: Water extinguishers are generally weaker than every other type of extinguisher and are not suitable for any type of fire
options.c: Water extinguishers may only be used by the fire brigade for insurance reasons
options.d: It does not matter which type of extinguisher is used, as long as it is within reach

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-03.explanation: Fires are classified by the type of burning material, including solids, liquids, gases, metals, and cooking oils/fats. With a burning fat fire, water can trigger a so-called fat explosion, producing a fireball and massively worsening the fire - specially approved fat-fire extinguishers exist for exactly this case. That is why it matters to know which extinguisher type suits which kind of fire.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-04.question: A colleague gets a minor cut on their finger and treats it themselves with a plaster from the first-aid box. They think nobody else needs to know. What is the usual principle for reporting incidents like this?

options.a: Minor injuries generally never need to be reported or documented at all
options.b: Even minor first-aid treatments should be recorded in the first-aid logbook, so that a connection to the work can be traced later if needed
options.c: A report is only required for a hospital stay of more than three days
options.d: Only the works council needs to be informed; no written documentation is intended

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-04.explanation: Even seemingly harmless injuries should be documented, for example in a first-aid logbook, because some consequences only become apparent later, and in a dispute - for instance with the accident insurer - it must be possible to prove that an injury was work-related. This protects the injured person themselves, in case what seemed like a small wound later develops into a more serious complication.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-01.question: An employee works at a screen continuously all day without a break. What does the Workplaces Ordinance (ArbStättV) fundamentally require here?

options.a: A fixed 15-minute break must occur after every full hour of screen work, without exception
options.b: There is no legal requirement whatsoever regarding interruptions during screen work
options.c: Screen work must be interrupted by other activities or recovery periods, with the specific arrangement to be determined as part of the risk assessment
options.d: An interruption is only legally required once daily screen work reaches ten hours

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-01.explanation: The Workplaces Ordinance requires that screen work be interrupted by other activities or recovery periods, but it does not prescribe a rigid schedule like exactly 15 minutes every hour. How the interruptions are actually arranged (mixed tasks, short breaks) is something the employer must determine for the specific workstation as part of the risk assessment.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-02.question: An employee at a typical screen workstation wants to know whether they are entitled to an eye examination. What applies?

options.a: An entitlement only exists once a medically confirmed vision impairment is already present
options.b: The employer must offer him what is called Angebotsvorsorge (offered preventive check-up); participation is voluntary but recommended
options.c: An eye examination is mandatory for every screen workstation and cannot be declined
options.d: An entitlement only exists for employees over the age of 50

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-02.explanation: For screen workstations, what is called Angebotsvorsorge applies: the employer must offer the examination, but the employee is not obliged to take part. In practice, most people do take up the offer, since vision problems caught early are usually easier to treat - neither an already-confirmed vision impairment nor reaching a certain minimum age is a precondition.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-03.question: The eye examination under the offered preventive check-up shows that an employee needs special screen-work glasses because their normal glasses are not sufficient for screen work. Who bears the cost of an appropriate pair of screen-work glasses?

options.a: The employer, provided the need was established through the occupational medical examination and a normal-standard model of glasses is chosen
options.b: The employee, since it is a private vision aid regardless of the reason
options.c: Statutory health insurance automatically covers the full cost of any glasses
options.d: There is no rule on this at all; the cost question is freely negotiable and legally completely open

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-03.explanation: If the occupational medical examination establishes that normal glasses are not sufficient for screen work, the employer must provide or pay for a special pair of screen-work glasses within a reasonable standard. Luxury frames or extras beyond that may fall to the employee, but the necessary basic provision is the employer's responsibility.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-04.question: Which of the following statements about the basic design of a screen workstation is correct?

options.a: Screen height and the distance to the employee play no relevant role for ergonomics
options.b: Glare and reflections on the screen from windows or lighting are irrelevant from an occupational safety standpoint
options.c: Ergonomic design is only required in permanently assigned individual offices, not in open-plan offices
options.d: The workstation should be designed to avoid disruptive glare and reflections, and the screen, keyboard, and seating should enable an ergonomically sound working posture

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-04.explanation: The requirements for screen work include avoiding glare and disruptive reflections on the screen, and designing and arranging the screen, keyboard, and seating so that an ergonomically favorable posture is possible. These requirements apply regardless of whether it is an individual office or an open-plan office.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-05.question: Employees repeatedly point out to their employer that a machine is missing a required guard. The employer still does nothing. What are the employees allowed to do under the Occupational Safety Act?

options.a: Contact the competent authority if the employer does nothing despite being informed - without this being held against them in any way
options.b: Nothing further, since only the works council is entitled to contact an authority
options.c: Only contact the authority after their employment has ended
options.d: Only contact the authority anonymously, without giving their name, since a named report is not permitted

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-05.explanation: Employees may make suggestions to the employer on safety and health matters. If the employer fails to adequately respond to concrete concerns, employees may contact the competent occupational safety authority directly - and this may explicitly not be held against them. Prior works council approval or even termination of employment are not preconditions for this.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-06.question: An employee notices a hazard and is unsure whether they may only tell their supervisor. Besides reporting to the employer, who else may employees inform about a hazard they have identified?

options.a: Also the occupational safety specialist, the company doctor, or the safety officer
options.b: Only the accident insurance carrier directly - there is no internal reporting channel
options.c: No one else - reporting to the supervisor is the only permitted route
options.d: Only once the hazard has already caused an accident

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-06.explanation: In addition to the duty to report to the employer or supervisor, employees should also be able to inform the occupational safety specialist, the company doctor, or the safety officer about hazards and defects they identify. This broadens the reporting channels but does not replace the duty to report without delay under §16(1) of the Occupational Safety Act.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-07.question: Because an experienced employee is off sick, an untrained temporary worker is to be assigned at short notice to a machine that normally requires special expertise. What does the Occupational Safety Act require when tasks are assigned like this?

options.a: The employer must first consider whether the person is capable of complying with the safety and health regulations that apply to that activity
options.b: It is enough that the temporary worker is willing to give it a try
options.c: This is permissible without further ado as long as the assignment lasts only a single day
options.d: The employer is relieved of all responsibility if the temporary worker voluntarily agreed to the assignment

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-07.explanation: When assigning tasks to employees, the employer must consider, depending on the type of activity, whether the person is actually capable of complying with the applicable safety and health regulations. Good intentions, a short assignment, or the temporary worker's voluntary agreement do not replace this assessment.

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-08.question: A company's management wants to effectively delegate part of its occupational safety duties to a senior employee. What does the Occupational Safety Act require for this to work?

options.a: A verbal agreement is enough, as long as both sides agree
options.b: A written assignment to a reliable and competent person who carries out the delegated tasks on their own responsibility
options.c: The tasks automatically pass to whichever present employee holds the highest rank
options.d: Delegation is fundamentally not permitted - management always remains solely responsible in every case

arbeitssicherheit-grundpflichten-08.explanation: The employer may formally assign, in writing, reliable and competent persons to carry out the employer's statutory occupational safety duties on their own responsibility. A mere verbal agreement or an automatic handover to the highest-ranking person present is not sufficient - and, contrary to a common assumption, delegation is in principle possible.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-05.question: A supervisor schedules the annual safety training for 6 p.m., after participants' official shift ends, so ongoing production is not disrupted. Is this allowed?

options.a: Yes, as long as the extra time is paid as overtime
options.b: No, the training must take place during employees' working hours
options.c: Yes, as long as attendance at this late slot remains voluntary
options.d: No, but only for full-time employees - part-time staff may be trained outside their agreed working hours

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-05.explanation: The Occupational Safety Act explicitly requires the employer to train employees during their working hours. Shifting it to after shift-end is not permitted even if overtime is paid or attendance is formally framed as voluntary - and the rule applies regardless of full-time or part-time status.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-06.question: Several colleagues in a warehouse have limited German skills. So far the safety training consists only of a complex, German-only handout to sign. Does this meet the requirements?

options.a: No, the content must be conveyed to employees in an understandable way for their specific work area - where there is a language barrier, the format must be adapted accordingly
options.b: Yes, as long as a signed training record exists at the end
options.c: Yes, legally it is sufficient to hand out the original German-language version
options.d: No, but only if more than half the workforce is affected by the language barrier

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-06.explanation: The employer must convey to employees, in an understandable way, the content of the accident prevention regulations relevant to their specific work area. A purely written, complex handout in a language that part of the workforce does not sufficiently understand fails this comprehensibility requirement - regardless of how many people are affected.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-07.question: An employee of an external window-cleaning company is deployed for a day in a production hall where hazardous substances are also handled. Who must make sure he has received adequate instructions about the hazards at the site?

options.a: Only his own employer, the window-cleaning company - the host site does not need to concern itself with this
options.b: The business where the work is actually carried out must, depending on the type of activity, make sure adequate instructions have been given
options.c: No one in particular - this is only addressed afterward if a workplace accident occurs
options.d: Such a duty only exists for assignments lasting longer than one week

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-07.explanation: When employees of several employers work at the same workplace, those employers must cooperate. The business where the activity is actually carried out must, depending on the type of work, make sure that employees of other employers have received adequate instructions about the hazards to their safety and health during their assignment - regardless of how long that assignment lasts.

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-08.question: After a near-miss, it turns out a new hazard on a machine was not covered in the last safety training, held only four months ago. Must the company wait until the next scheduled annual training?

options.a: No, the training must be repeated immediately whenever necessary - regardless of the annual minimum cycle
options.b: Yes, the annual minimum frequency may not be broken within a single year
options.c: Yes, unless an actual injury has already occurred
options.d: No, but only if the competent accident insurance carrier explicitly orders it

arbeitssicherheit-unterweisung-08.explanation: Training must be repeated whenever necessary, but at least once a year. The annual cycle is therefore a floor, not a ceiling: if a new hazard emerges, retraining must happen without delay, regardless of when the last regular training took place or whether anyone has already been injured.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: A retail business has 30 nearly identical checkout workstations with the same tasks, equipment, and working conditions. Must a separate hazard assessment be created for every single checkout workstation?

options.a: Yes, every single workplace absolutely requires its own fully separate assessment
options.b: No, for identical or comparable working conditions, an assessment of one workplace or activity is sufficient
options.c: Yes, but only if the business has more than 20 comparable workplaces in total
options.d: No, a single general assessment for the whole business with no reference to specific activities is always sufficient

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must carry out the hazard assessment according to the type of activities involved. Where working conditions are comparable, assessing one workplace or activity is sufficient - neither a mandatory individual assessment for every identical workplace nor a completely activity-independent blanket assessment for the whole business is required.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: A small company with 8 employees believes it is too small to have to document the results of its hazard assessment at all. Is that correct?

options.a: Yes, businesses with fewer than 10 employees are generally exempt from any documentation duty
options.b: No, the documentation duty exists regardless of a fixed employee threshold - its scope depends on the type of activities and the size of the business, but it does not disappear entirely
options.c: Yes, a documentation duty only generally exists from 20 employees upward
options.d: No, however the documentation may be purely verbal and does not need to exist in writing

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must keep the documents required depending on the type of activities and the number of employees, showing the result of the hazard assessment, the measures determined, and the result of their review. The law does not provide for a fixed employee number above which this duty disappears entirely - though where hazard situations are comparable, a consolidated documentation is sufficient.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: An employee falls at work and is on sick leave for five working days as a result. Must the employer document this accident separately?

options.a: Yes, accidents resulting in death or in incapacity for work of more than three days must be recorded by the employer
options.b: No, reporting to the accident insurance carrier is enough - an additional internal record is not required
options.c: No, a documentation duty legally only exists once incapacity for work exceeds seven days
options.d: Yes, but only if a third party is found to be at fault

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must record accidents suffered by employees at work if an employee is killed or is unable to work for more than three days. This is a distinct documentation duty alongside any report to the accident insurance carrier, and does not depend on whether a third party is at fault.

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.question: An intern with no relevant expertise is asked by management to quickly draw up the hazard assessment for a new workshop. Is this permissible?

options.a: Yes, as long as some document titled 'hazard assessment' exists at the end
options.b: Yes, as long as a supervisor formally countersigns the finished assessment afterward
options.c: No, the hazard assessment must be carried out by suitably qualified personnel; if the necessary expertise is not available in-house, competent expert advice must be obtained
options.d: No, it may only be prepared by an external government authority

arbeitssicherheit-gefaehrdungsbeurteilun.explanation: The employer must ensure that the assessment of hazards arising from the workplace is carried out by suitably qualified personnel. If the business itself lacks the necessary expertise, it must obtain competent advice. A mere subsequent countersignature by a supervisor without the relevant expertise does not substitute for this requirement.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-05.question: An administrative business has 45 employees present. What is the minimum number of trained first aiders that must be maintained under the applicable requirements?

options.a: At least 5% of employees present, so at least 3 first aiders here
options.b: At least 10% of employees present, so at least 5 first aiders here
options.c: Always exactly one first aider, regardless of the number of employees
options.d: This is not legally regulated and is entirely at the employer's discretion

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-05.explanation: Where more than 20 employees are present, administrative and retail businesses must have at least 5% trained and available as first aiders, while other businesses (e.g. production) require at least 10%. For 45 employees in an administrative business, that works out to at least 3 first aiders - the 10% rate applies to other types of business, not to administration.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-06.question: A company issued protective gloves but does not follow up afterward: worn, partly torn gloves have hung on the same hook for months and are still being used. Does this meet the employer's obligations?

options.a: Yes, once PPE has been provided once, further care is solely the employees' responsibility
options.b: No, the employer must, through maintenance, repair, and replacement where necessary, ensure the PPE remains functional and hygienically sound throughout its entire period of use
options.c: Yes, a duty to replace only arises after a fixed statutory period of five years
options.d: No, a maintenance duty legally only applies to respiratory protective equipment, not to simple protective gloves

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-06.explanation: The employer must, through maintenance, repair, replacement measures, and suitable storage, ensure that personal protective equipment functions well and remains in a hygienically sound condition throughout its entire period of use. This duty does not end once the equipment has been issued, and it is not limited to specific types of PPE such as respiratory protection.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-07.question: A green, rectangular sign with a white pictogram of a running figure and an arrow pointing to a door hangs in a corridor. What does this marking indicate?

options.a: A rescue sign, for example marking an escape route or emergency exit
options.b: A mandatory sign requiring a specific action, such as wearing hearing protection
options.c: A prohibition sign forbidding a specific action, such as smoking
options.d: A warning sign cautioning about a general source of danger

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-07.explanation: Safety signage follows a fixed system of shape and color: rescue signs for escape and rescue routes are rectangular or square and green with a white pictogram. Mandatory signs, by contrast, are round and blue, prohibition signs are round with a red border, and warning signs are triangular and yellow - a running figure on a green background clearly belongs to the rescue sign category.

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-08.question: A fire extinguisher in a corridor was last inspected over two years ago. The caretaker wants to quickly clear it himself with a brief visual check. Does this meet the requirements?

options.a: Yes, a visual check by trained in-house staff is generally sufficient for any inspection
options.b: Yes, fire extinguishers only need to be inspected if they have actually been used
options.c: No, fire extinguishers must generally be inspected at least every two years by a competent, qualified person - a simple visual check by an untrained person is not sufficient
options.d: No, the prescribed inspection interval is five years; a two-year cycle would be excessively frequent

arbeitssicherheit-psa_notfall-08.explanation: Portable fire extinguishers must generally be inspected regularly, at least every two years, by a competent, qualified person - not by just any in-house staff performing a simple visual check. This inspection also detects hidden defects that a superficial glance would miss, and it is required regardless of whether the extinguisher has ever actually been used.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-05.question: An employer installs software that secretly evaluates each person's keystrokes per minute, without the employees' knowledge. Is this permitted under the rules for designing screen workstations?

options.a: Yes, as long as the collected data is not used for formal warnings
options.b: No, monitoring of work results in terms of quantity or quality may not take place without the employees' knowledge
options.c: Yes, if the works council is informed about the evaluation afterward
options.d: No, but only if personally identifiable data is stored in the data-protection-law sense while doing so

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-05.explanation: The rules on designing screen workstations expressly prohibit monitoring work results in terms of quantity or quality without the employees' knowledge. This applies regardless of what the evaluation is later used for or whether the works council is informed afterward - what matters is that employees did not know about the monitoring at the time it took place.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-06.question: An employee worries that her monitor emits 'dangerous radiation' like an old CRT screen and wants an extra lead curtain in front of it. What does the Workplace Ordinance actually require regarding radiation from screen devices?

options.a: Electromagnetic radiation from screen devices must be kept low enough that employees' safety and health are not endangered - standard modern devices meet this without any extra shielding
options.b: Screen devices at the workplace must fundamentally emit no radiation at all
options.c: An individual radiation measurement by an external expert must be commissioned for every single screen workstation
options.d: Additional shielding devices such as lead or metal curtains are mandatory for all screen workstations

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-06.explanation: The requirements demand that electromagnetic radiation from screen devices be kept low enough that no danger to safety and health arises - not that no radiation may occur at all. Standard modern screens meet this requirement without any additional individual measurements or shielding devices such as lead curtains.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-07.question: A new employee starts work at a typical screen workstation and has had no vision complaints so far. At the earliest, when must the offer of screen-work health check-ups be made to him?

options.a: Already before he starts working at screen devices, and then again regularly afterward - not only once complaints arise
options.b: Only after he has complained of vision problems
options.c: Only after his probationary period in the company has ended
options.d: Only at the works council's explicit request, not automatically for every new employee

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-07.explanation: The offer of occupational health check-ups for screen work must already be made before the employee starts working at screen devices, and must then be repeated at regular intervals afterward. It is designed to be preventive and must not be offered only once complaints have already arisen or once the probationary period ends.

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-08.question: An employee cannot achieve an ergonomically sound sitting posture despite a correctly adjusted chair and desk, and asks for a footrest. Must the employer grant this request?

options.a: Yes, at the employee's request a footrest must be provided if an ergonomically sound posture cannot otherwise be achieved
options.b: No, footrests are purely comfort items and providing them is entirely at the employer's discretion
options.c: Yes, but only if an occupational health examination has explicitly confirmed the problem beforehand
options.d: No, this is purely a matter for a voluntary works agreement and is not legally regulated

arbeitssicherheit-bildschirmarbeit-08.explanation: At the employees' request, the employer must provide a footrest and a document holder if an ergonomically favorable working posture cannot otherwise be achieved. A prior occupational health confirmation or a separate works agreement are not preconditions for this.
